analyst_view.overall: Early view: Ferencvaros are one of three teams on a perfect 12 points and were on a 20-match unbeaten run under Balazs Borbely when they won 2-0 at San Siro. Celje (25th, 4 points) sit just outside the play-off places after a 3-2 win at Sturm Graz, so both sides have plenty to play for.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.1 goals. I lean a little higher: Ferencvaros have scored at least twice in every league-phase game and won their two home games 2-1 and 4-1, while Celje's last two games produced nine goals (2-2 with Salzburg, 3-2 at Sturm). Ferencvaros lose Bamidele Yusuf, sent off at Milan, and Celje miss Artemijus Tutyskinas through suspension.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.3 corners. Ferencvaros should have more of the ball at home and Celje showed at Sturm that they will attack, so corners should come at both ends, which matches the site's split.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.2 cards. Ferencvaros finished with ten men at Milan after Yusuf's off-the-ball elbow on Mario Gila, and UEFA may add to his ban for violent conduct, but that was a one-off; neither side's games have been bad-tempered, so I stay with the number.

shots.text: The numbers say 25.2 shots. With Ferencvaros chasing a top-eight finish and Celje willing to attack, a total in the mid-20s fits.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.6 shots on target. I lean slightly higher: both sides have been finishing well lately (Lenny Joseph's double at Milan, Svit Seslar's two at Sturm), and Celje's open games suggest chances at both ends.
